mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL and depressed TRANSIT indicate ongoing stay-at-home behavior and reduced trip generation, which directly suppresses discretionary retail visits and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 17.7 and TRANSIT is -67.0 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 and TRANSIT remains below -60.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT collapse below -65 removes a large share of non-essential retail trips, so RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -65 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: After TRANSIT closes below -65, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than its previous 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden collapse in PARKS combined with negative GROCERY_PHARM signals households cutting all non-essential trips, and the interaction amplifies the fall in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 20 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM is negative
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS drops from -11.7 to -35.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS falls more than 20 points and GROCERY_PHARM is negative, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days rises rather than falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime with high residential mobility, stabilization in WORKPLACES and elevated RESIDENTIAL signal that the worst of the mobility contraction is passing, which lifts discretionary retail over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stabilizes from -33.0 to -32.3 and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated at 17.7
failure_condition: In reopening-with-high-residential regimes, when WORKPLACES stabilizes and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July seasonal heat and vacation patterns reduce park-based and outdoor social trips, which spill over into lower discretionary retail activity over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is -35.7 in t-0w after falling from -11.7 in t-1w
failure_condition: During the summer season, when PARKS remains below -30, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than its previous 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deep contractions in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate a lockdown-like regime that removes commuter and transit-dependent retail demand, driving RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -60 and WORKPLACES < -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below -60 and -30 from t-2w through t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT < -60 and WORKPLACES < -30 for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in RETAIL_REC greater than 8 points signals a negative footfall feedback loop, so RETAIL_REC continues lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC drops from -31.3 to -40.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: After a >8-point weekly fall in RETAIL_REC, the next week's RETAIL_REC is higher than the current level.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-peak reopening regime, if TRANSIT stops falling while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, pent-up demand for retail and recreation produces a rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stabilizes above -70 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -67.0 and RESIDENTIAL is 17.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stabilizes above -70 while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.
